To my understanding this is not allowed in the Redfish spec.  200 should return the current state of the resource.  204 is allowed to return with no body.
PATCH is expected to return the current state of the resource. so, after a successful PATCH the correct status code (200 ok) with a successful response body is returned
Acknowledged
Either work.. why do we want 200?
We want 200 OK in this case because the PATCH operation returns a response body after successfully updating the event service fields

I am looking at 7.5.1. Modification success responses

https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0266_1.8.0.pdf

```
For update, replace, and delete operations, the response from the service, after successful modification,
should be one of the following responses:
• HTTP 200 status code with a body that contains the JSON representation of the targeted resource after the modification has been applied, or, for the delete operation, a representation of
the deleted resource.
```

So without a body that contains the targeted resource this is wrong.
As per document I updated the response body
Acknowledged
Why is this better than just returning 204 ?
204 No Content response without detailed info about what fields were updated, Becuase , if apply a patch to update event service fields, certain fields (like retryAttempts) have value constraints
Acknowledged

Will update the commit message with the details
Acknowledged
Let's do this as a separate commit if you want to refactor this, it makes reviewing the actual change too hard
I hope without this response body change here this refactor change no needed

Why do we need this?

Currently, when applying a patch to event service fields, certain fields have strict value limits (e.g., retryAttempts must be between 1 and 3). If an invalid value is provided, the API returns an error, making it easy to identify the issue. However, in the success case, the API does not provide explicit confirmation of the updated values, so it's hard to verify what changed without fetching the resource again
